text:
sam: Heads up — small repro for an annoying Vite + TS SDK issue. When running a local dev server with HMR on Windows, a dynamic import of the SDK sometimes resolves to the package's CJS file and the browser throws a module specifier error. filing this so we can add to the DX playbook. repo: https://git.internal/repro/vite-hmr-sdk-windows

lee: can you share minimal steps? wondering if it's HMR only or also build step

sam: super minimal:
1) git clone the repo above
2) yarn install && yarn dev (vite)
3) open http://localhost:3000 and click the "call sdk" button

The app uses this tiny lazy import in src/app.tsx:
```ts
// lazy load to simulate code-splitting/HMR
const client = await import('redwood-inference');
await client.generate({ prompt: 'hello' });
```
Console error in Chromium on Windows: 
```
Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: Failed to resolve module specifier: "../node_modules/redwood-inference/dist/index.cjs.js"
    at Module.eval (app.tsx:10)
```

nina: that path looks wrong for ESM. My hunch: Vite's resolver during dev sometimes follows "require" entry in exports map for dynamic imports, especially when path normalization on Windows yields backslashes and the dev server's file URL mapping confuses the ESM loader. Does the package.json have both import and require in its exports?

sam: yes, package.json in node_modules has both. quick local test: editing node_modules/redwood-inference/package.json and removing the require entry makes the error go away. diff I used:
```diff
-  "exports": {
-    "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
-    "require": "./dist/index.cjs.js"
-  },
+  "exports": {
+    "import": "./dist/index.mjs"
+  },
```
But obviously we can't ship that change to users.

lee: workaround ideas: 1) add the package to optimizeDeps.include so Vite prebundles it (prevents dynamic resolver decision), 2) set resolve.conditions to favor 'import', or 3) use an explicit ESM import instead of dynamic import. Any of those work?

sam: I tested optimizeDeps.include and resolve.conditions = ['import'] — both stop the error. downside: resolve.conditions affects module resolution for other deps and can hide other issues; optimizeDeps prebundling changes HMR semantics a bit. Also TypeScript intellisense in VSCode got weird after forcing import-only resolution — some type paths started pointing at cjs d.ts shims.

nina: sounds like two separate DX problems to document: (A) bundler/runtime mismatch where conditional exports + dynamic import + Windows path normalization pick the wrong target; (B) TS types bridging CJS shims causing IDE/type mismatch when forcing import-only resolution. We should add a small sample app with each workaround and explanation.

sam: I'll create a short devex note + sample with three configs: vite.config.ts optimized, resolve.conditions example, and an explicit import shim approach (import * as SDK from 'redwood-inference/dist/index.mjs'). I'll also add a Windows note about backslash -> URL mapping affecting resolver internals. cc @nina for wording.

qa-bot: created ticket DEVEX-4829: "vite HMR dynamic import resolves CJS target for redwood-inference on Windows; add repro and workarounds""
